needs_human.note: When a row already holds the target path, the file moves but its own row stays at the old path (fileops.py:403-412, pinned by `test_row_holding_the_target_path_stays_and_the_rename_succeeds`). At the next scan, by reading the code, the stale row at the target recovers and takes over the file with its old tags and history, while the uploaded row is flagged missing.; A batch rename with `clip_{n}` that selects a video and its uploaded subtitle numbers them separately, for example `clip_1.mp4` and `clip_2.srt`, so the track detaches with a 200. The dialog offers no way to keep the pair together.; A trashed subtitle row follows its file, because `_follow_sidecar_row` applies no state filter (fileops.py:396-400), so it stays trashed at the new path and possibly on another drive. Addon reactions to the subtitle row were not traced.

After the scanner fix, an uploaded subtitle stays in the listing as its own card through rescans, while a subtitle placed on disk never has one. The same file therefore looks different by origin. decisions.md:33 and :46 observed the card, and the user guide says subtitles do not appear in the file list.; Databases where a rescan already flagged uploaded subtitles missing will see them recover as cards on the next scan after this change, with a files.recovered event for each.; A subtitle row that follows its video is not named in the files.moved event (routers/files.py:381 and :435 emit only the video ids), and a row whose path the carry changed gets no event of its own. Intelligence documents a reconcile for missed events (addons/intelligence/app/indexer.py:374), but other subscribers were not traced.; Video and sidecar are not committed together.
